To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EEG power of the delta and beta bands are inversely related to the FC of the DMN and that this EEG pattern has previously been linked to alertness.

A network- and frequency-specific relation between DMN FC and EEG was identified, which was characterized by an EEG pattern previously associated with increased arousal and by the established SEF95 sedation index.
we identified a network and frequency-specific association between intrinsic FC of the DMN and a distinct EEG signature, which was previously associated with increased vigilance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel EEG/fMRI correlation method.
the development of a new approach for the analysis of combined EEG/fMRI data.
the neurophysiological correlates of functional connectivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study provides evidence for a distinct EEG pattern that is related to intrinsic FC of the default mode network (and possibly of other networks).
the EEG power spectrum is a good predictor of DMN functional connectivity.
the DMN FC is related to the alertness of a subject.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the slow EEG pattern (delta and beta) is a neurophysiological correlate to DMN FC.
the DMN is associated with a slow EEG signature, which in turn is related to increased FC.
we have demonstrated that a slow EEG pattern is related to reduced intrinsic functional connectivity of the default mode network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EEG can be used to study intrinsic FC in a network-specific fashion.
a slow EEG pattern predicts reduced FC in the DMN.
the EEG signature of the DMN is a slow pattern of delta and beta oscillations.
